name: Raycast dungeon
oneLiner: A first-person grid dungeon crawler drawn by raycasting: one DDA ray per screen column with the perpendicular distance (no fisheye, no gaps), 64 x 64 code-drawn wall textures per theme (brick cellars, mossy halls, a basalt vault with glowing seams), torch walls with animated flames that light the cells around them, banners, doors that slide open in the middle of their cell, a stair arch, cast floors and ceilings, distance fog and a lantern; monsters and items are billboards drawn column by column against the wall depth, with idle, wind-up, strike and hurt frames, a solid white hit flash and a sidestep on a miss. The hero steps one cell and turns 90 degrees with smooth tweens, strikes what stands in front with a first-person sword, opens doors, drinks tonics, takes the stairs; every step, strike or wait is a turn after which every awake monster moves or attacks. Seeded floors (rooms, maze corridors, loops, doors, torches) or floors from data, a minimap and a full map, a HUD, a message log, combat labels that never cover a character or the HUD, and a bot that plays through the same rules.
fits: a dungeon mode inside an RPG or an adventure game
retro 2.5D games that want a pseudo-3D view without WebGL
notFor: free-moving first-person action (the hero steps on a grid)
games that need height, stairs inside the view or sloped floors (one floor height)
side-view or top-down games (use B-12 dungeon floors for a top-down crawl)

needs: a seed per run and a fixed 60 Hz update step (turns are input-driven; tweens and animations run on the step)
key or tap input routed to the dungeon while it runs (forward, back, turn, step aside, strike, wait, tonic, map) and held keys
a canvas 2D context and a logical view rect, ideally an integer number of device px per art px
optional: monsters, items and hand-made floors as data
a place to go when the run is won or lost
provides: the floors: rooms, maze corridors, loops, doors, torch and banner walls, a stair arch, monsters and items by budget, a boss on the last floor; or floors from rows of characters
the rules: grid steps and 90 degree turns, bump to strike or open, hits with evade / crit / defence, monster wake, chase and erratic steps, speed, XP and levels, tonics

the view: DDA raycaster (perpendicular distance, one ray per column), textured walls, sliding doors, cast floors and ceilings, torch light map, lantern, fog, billboards with per-column depth, the first-person sword with idle, wind-up, strike and hurt poses
the screen: HUD (HP, tonics, gold, level, floor, compass), minimap, full map, message log, floor banner, combat labels beside their owner, hurt vignette and hit-direction marks
hit site onHit on the impact frame (read-only), onEvent (floorStart, turn, move, attack, wake, door, death, pickup, potion, heal, levelUp, descend, end), onEnd(result, info)
a bot that explores, fights, loots and descends through the same rules
anchors (monster billboard boxes, the hero's sword), unit rects, UI rects, field rect, labels, actors() text state, pure castColumns / renderView for tools

params.label: Share of room openings with a door
Combat labels (off when an addon draws its own)

assets: module/raycast-dungeon.js (global GameDNA_RaycastDungeon, no dependencies; API in module/README.md). Everything is made in code at load time: 64 x 64 textures for brick, mossy stone and basalt walls, torch walls (3 flame frames), banners, the door, the stair arch, flagstone, mossy and cinder floors, beam and rock ceilings; billboards for the Gloom Slime, Cave Bat, Grave Knight and the Mire King (idle, wind-up, strike, hurt) and three item looks; the first-person sword in six poses; the 7 px pixel font (shared design with B-12 / C-03). No image files, no new generated art.
